title: GoldenLoaf's delayed orders
prompt: GoldenLoaf supplies fresh bread and pastries to grocery stores across the Midwest. Customer demand remains healthy, but on-time order fulfillment has fallen from 94% to 78% over the past six months. Management wants to restore service without committing to a major facility expansion.
objective: Identify the operational bottleneck behind GoldenLoaf's late orders and recommend a practical way to restore capacity and service levels.

clarificationOptions.label: Which service outcome should we improve?
clarificationOptions.response: Focus on restoring on-time order fulfillment from 78% toward its prior 94% level.

clarificationOptions.label: Which facilities and customers are in scope?
clarificationOptions.response: The issue is concentrated in GoldenLoaf's main bakery, which serves all of the affected grocery customers.

clarificationOptions.label: What investment constraints should we respect?
clarificationOptions.response: Management will consider modest operating changes or targeted equipment, but wants to avoid a major facility expansion.

clarificationOptions.label: Have competitors increased promotions?
clarificationOptions.response: Competitor promotions have not materially affected GoldenLoaf's order volume or fulfillment performance.

facts.text: On-time order fulfillment fell from 94% to 78% over six months, while cancellations remained low.
Average demand is 840 trays per day and reaches about 900 trays from Tuesday through Thursday.
Daily effective capacity is 1,200 trays in mixing, 1,100 in proofing, 760 in baking, and 1,050 in packaging.
The ovens run at 98% utilization during scheduled hours; every other production stage remains at or below 76%.
Work-in-process accumulates before the ovens, while packaging is frequently idle waiting for baked product.
Small-batch premium products increased from 18% to 34% of tray volume and remain profitable and strategically important.
Oven changeovers increased from 14 to 24 per week as the product mix shifted toward smaller batches.
Cleaning and temperature resets now consume about eight oven hours per week, reducing effective baking capacity to 760 trays per day.
A two-week pilot grouping products by bake temperature reduced changeovers by 38% and raised effective oven capacity to 880 trays per day without affecting quality.
The sequencing pilot covers average demand but leaves a roughly 20-tray gap on peak weekdays.
Four flexible oven hours on peak weekdays would add approximately 45 trays of capacity per day using existing equipment.
Production staffing is 97% filled, absenteeism is unchanged, and labor coverage is adequate at each stage.
Ingredient availability exceeds the production plan, and supplier fill rates remain above 98%.

investigationNodes.label: Inspect the fulfillment decline
investigationNodes.interviewerResponse: On-time fulfillment has fallen sharply, but customers are generally waiting rather than canceling orders.

investigationNodes.label: Review daily demand
investigationNodes.interviewerResponse: Average demand is 840 trays per day, with a Tuesday-through-Thursday peak near 900 trays.

investigationNodes.label: Compare capacity by production stage
investigationNodes.interviewerResponse: Baking has materially less effective capacity than mixing, proofing, or packaging. The process-capacity exhibit is now available.

investigationNodes.label: Inspect oven utilization and queues
investigationNodes.interviewerResponse: The ovens are nearly fully utilized, with a queue before baking and idle time after it.

investigationNodes.label: Review the recent product-mix shift
investigationNodes.interviewerResponse: Small-batch premium products have nearly doubled their volume share. They are profitable, so simply removing them would sacrifice attractive business.

investigationNodes.label: Analyze oven changeovers
investigationNodes.interviewerResponse: More small batches have driven oven changeovers from 14 to 24 per week, consuming eight hours and reducing effective baking capacity. The changeover exhibit is now available.

investigationNodes.label: Review the production-sequencing pilot
investigationNodes.interviewerResponse: Grouping products by bake temperature cut changeovers by 38% and lifted effective oven capacity to 880 trays per day without harming quality.

investigationNodes.label: Evaluate peak-day coverage
investigationNodes.interviewerResponse: A small flexible-hours extension would close the remaining peak-day gap using the current ovens.

investigationNodes.label: Check production staffing
investigationNodes.interviewerResponse: Staffing and attendance are stable, and labor coverage is adequate across the production line.

investigationNodes.label: Check ingredient availability
investigationNodes.interviewerResponse: Ingredients are readily available and supplier fill rates remain above 98%, so supply is not constraining output.

exhibits.title: Effective daily capacity by production stage

insights.label: Baking is the binding production constraint.
Packaging is the binding production constraint.
Frequent changeovers are suppressing effective oven capacity.
The sequencing pilot increased capacity by accepting lower quality.

decisions.label: Group production by bake temperature and add flexible oven hours on peak weekdays before considering new equipment.
Discontinue all small-batch premium products immediately.
Purchase a second packaging line to increase downstream capacity.

risks.label: Longer production runs could make it harder to meet freshness windows for some products.
Demand spikes above the current peak could exceed the added flexible capacity.
Flexible oven hours could strain the trained oven team if scheduling is not rotated.

nextSteps.label: Run a four-week sequencing and flexible-hours rollout while tracking on-time fulfillment, oven capacity, and quality.
Issue an immediate request for proposals for a second packaging line.
Notify customers that premium products will be discontinued next month.

efficientPaths.label: Find the bottleneck, then recover effective capacity
Size demand and mix before isolating the oven constraint
